needle_mechanical_controls.interpretation: Official nonfirst tool, default/explicit-weight routes, stateless controls and enum/opaque-ID controls work. These are separate mechanical diagnostics after primary English results; primary corpus, gates and scored outputs were not changed. The cause of all game-case abstentions is not established.

limitations: Newly authored synthetic cases measure explicit instruction and constraint compliance, not gameplay success, real-world memory retrieval quality, or general model accuracy.
English/Japanese pairs are translations; 24 cases represent 12 semantic questions, and 6 commander cases represent only 3 missions.
Memory relevance here requires useful new information. Explicitly superseded or duplicate information is labeled false under a stated policy, even if topically related.
Commander choices are three complete predefined plans under explicit role constraints; no free plan generation, future simulation or combat strength is measured.

Needle primary suites used localized schemas and common system facts plus raw instructions, fixed before its corpus outputs. Public mechanical probes were kept separate. Suppressed calls were never promoted to accepted actions.
Needle returned normal successful envelopes but abstained on all 24 scored requests. Safe handling on the six clarify cases does not imply useful coverage of executable commands.

Official docs describe a 0.1 confidence floor or grounding gate; actual native suppression is preserved. A confidence above 0.1 alone does not prove a call will be issued, and the exact suppression cause was not established.
Hindsight CPU adapter uses unchanged released render/alias-max/softmax/answer code and original weights. vLLM server/kernel numerical parity, GPU and Unity execution are not measured.

TinyJev uses native FP32/Torch2.7.1/Transformers5.3 and its fixed trained head temperature1.4640856959456252; Hindsight uses BF16/Torch2.9.1/Transformers5.19 and official T1 alias reduction. Different templates/token counts/dtypes/backends prevent architecture-only speed or memory claims.

Needle parent and native-worker RSS are reported separately. RSS includes runtime state and is not model-only allocation or VRAM. One warmup and one timed pass do not establish a latency distribution.
